message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What You’re Generally Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|-----------------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord keeps any portion. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.). | • Report problems in writing (email or letter).
• If the landlord fails to fix, you may withhold rent, repair and deduct, or pursue a “repair‑and‑deduct” claim in small‑claims court. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hrs) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of any entries; if the landlord enters without notice, you can file a complaint. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30‑day written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, you can break the lease only if the landlord breaches the lease or if you have a “just cause” (e.g., landlord fails to maintain habitability). | • Provide written notice and keep copies. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the Texas eviction procedure (notice, court filing, judgment, sheriff’s execution). | • Respond to notices promptly; you can contest the eviction in court. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major problem, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent, provided you follow the proper procedure. | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report disturbances; if unresolved, seek mediation or legal action. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord cannot monitor your activities inside the unit without consent. | • If you suspect surveillance, document and seek legal counsel. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Lease may restrict subletting; if allowed, you must follow the lease terms. | • Obtain written permission; keep records. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise specified. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must keep common areas clean and safe. | • Report issues; if ignored, you may withhold rent or take action. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Small‑claims court (up to $20,000) for disputes over deposits, repairs, or unpaid rent.
• Texas Attorney General’s Office or local housing agencies for complaints. | • File claims, keep documentation, and consider mediation. | ### Quick Tips for Protecting Your Rights 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – All obligations and rights are spelled out there. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written communication, and receipts. 3. **Keep Copies of All Notices** – Move‑in inspection, rent receipts, notices of entry, etc. 4. **Know the Timeline** – Notice periods, deposit return deadlines, and court deadlines. 5. **Seek Help Early** – Contact local tenant‑rights groups, legal aid, or the Texas Commission on Human Rights if you suspect discrimination or unlawful practices. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Information on landlord‑tenant disputes, consumer rights, and how to file complaints. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | Handles discrimination complaints. | | **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** | Provides guidance on fair housing and tenant rights. | | **Local Legal Aid Organizations** | Free or low‑cost legal assistance for tenants. | | **Texas Small Claims Court** | Process for filing claims up to $20,000. | If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a security deposit, a landlord refusing to make repairs, or a potential eviction notice), let me know and I can give more tailored guidance or help draft a letter to your landlord.
